messages:
ashley-support: FYI just got an escalated support ticket from ACME. They've been seeing p95/p99 regressions after we turned on tool/function calling + strict JSON schema validation for outputs. Root: latency single-digit -> double-digit at p99 for some requests. Posting sample request and perf traces below.

ashley-support: Customer repro: curl against our hosted API with a tool router and a JSON schema to force structured output. They say it was fine until ~2026-03-10 rollout of the 'structured-validation' flag.

ashley-support: repro curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDCAB_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.2","input":"Summarize sales, call tools","tools":[{"name":"sales-db","schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"region":{"type":"string"},"top_customers":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"name":{"type":"string"},"rev":{"type":"number"}}}}}}]}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

ashley-support: Customer metrics (their telemetry + our traces): p50 ~ 450ms, p95 jumped 1.8s -> 3.6s, p99 jumped 3.2s -> 9.7s after the flag. They attached span breakdowns showing big time in two places: `tool_router` and `json_validator`.

luca-runtime: On it. Do we have the raw spans from our tracing ingest? If so paste trace IDs. Also which region? Could be a routing hot path.

ashley-support: Trace IDs: trace-0a1b2c3d, trace-0a1b2c9f (attached). Region: us-west-2. Customer traffic pattern is many small calls with heavy schema checks (arrays of objects).

priya-sre: pulling traces now. Early look: in those traces model token generation is normal (~250-400ms), but `router.dispatch_tools` shows 700-1400ms and `output.json_validator` 400-1200ms in many p99 traces. Combined those explain the p99 jump. Also seeing queueing spikes on the tool-router worker pool during the canary.

kevin-platform: That matches the hypothesis from rollout notes — we enabled synchronous validaton during tool routing for stronger guarantees. Seems the validation is doing recursive schema validation for each tool result in the request thread. For arrays with many elements it can be O(n*m) where n=items, m=properties.

luca-runtime: Quick triage checklist: 1) Can we reproduce locally with their payload? 2) Can we bypass validation per-customer via a header? 3) Add instrumentation to measure per-elem validation time.

ashley-support: Customer willing to test a bypass header. They want minimal change quickly.

priya-sre: For immediate mitigation I'd recommend: a) enable per-route short-circuit: if header `X-Redwood-Skip-Output-Validation: 1` then we skip strict JSON schema validation and mark request `validation=skipped` in traces; b) increase tool-router worker pool temporarily for their account; c) set a 5s soft timeout on router to avoid p99 > 10s. These are low-risk.

luca-runtime: I can patch the router to honor the header and set a feature-flag gated patch. Will do a canary to 5% first. Also will add a cheap guard: if schema `maxItems` or `patternProperties` absent we use a faster shallow check.

kevin-platform: Good — add a metric `validation.type=fast|full|skipped` so we can break down latencies. Also log schema size (#properties, maxItems).

luca-runtime: Repro locally using customer's example: confirmed. With full validation p99 ~ 3.8s on dev box, skipping validation drops p99 to ~650ms. Quick local snippet of flamegraph sample from our profiler:
```
# simplified stack samples (ms)
router.dispatch_tools 1200
  -> tool.call (network) 300
  -> output.json_validator 800
    -> json-schema.checkObject 450
    -> json-schema.checkArrayItems 300
```

luca-runtime: Root cause: synchronous, recursive, per-tool JSON schema validation is serial and not batched. For multi-tool pipelines or tools returning arrays we do repeated expensive checks on the runtime thread.

priya-sre: Two follow-up actions: short-term mitigations and long-term fixes. Short-term: header bypass + bump worker pool + fail-open timeout. Long-term: move validation to async validation worker, return streaming partial response with `validation_pending` flag, add incremental validation and cache compiled schemas per-account+version.

ashley-support: Customer agreed to header bypass to test now. They also asked for timeline for permanent fix.

luca-runtime: I'll open a PR for header bypass + metric + canary config. ETA: 4h to dev + 2h to canary rollout. If canary looks good we can increase to 100% in 48h.

kevin-platform: I'll provision a temporary routing autoscale for their account and add a temporary throttle to background validation queue to prevent router starvation.

priya-sre: I'll watch traces during canary and set an alert if p99 spikes > 2x baseline. I'll also collect `validation.duration` histogram.

ashley-support: Customer will test bypass now and report. I gave them a header: `X-Redwood-Skip-Output-Validation: 1` and a test endpoint for canary (us-west-2).

dev-bot: deploy-event: PR #5423 (router: honor X-Redwood-Skip-Output-Validation) deployed to canary (5%) in us-west-2 at 2026-03-15T15:23:12Z :rocket:

luca-runtime: Can everyone check the canary traces: trace ids start with c0ffee-*. Priya?

priya-sre: Canary samples show for bypassed requests p95 ~ 520ms, p99 ~ 780ms. Non-bypassed still high; matches expectation. No error increase. Good signal.

luca-runtime: Next steps (action items):
- luca-runtime: Merge hotfix to routing to support header and fast-path, add `validation.type` metric. (in progress)
- kevin-platform: Temporary autoscale + throttle for ACME account. (done)
- priya-sre: Monitor p95/p99, add alert. (watching)
- ashley-support: coordinate with customer and confirm when they want full rollback to pre-rollout behavior or permanent config. (on standby)

kevin-platform: For the longer term I'll start a spec for async validation worker + schema cache. We should also consider returning a preflight `validate=true/false` suggestion in SDKs so customers can opt in to strict validation with guidelines.

luca-runtime: Also proposal: implement a fast-compiled validator path (WASM or JIT compiled) for common schema shapes. Might cut validation time by 4-10x. Adding to roadmap.

ashley-support: ACME says bypass reduced their p99 to acceptable range. They want us to keep bypass on for now while we do staged improvements.

priya-sre: I'll keep this thread updated with dashboards and trace snippets. If anyone finds regressions in other accounts we should open a separate incident.

luca-runtime: I'll post PR link here when merged.

dev-bot: pr-merge: PR #5423 merged to main by luca-runtime at 2026-03-15T18:02:54Z

luca-runtime: PR merged. Rolling canary to 25% then 100% for ACME. Leaving feature-flag window for 48h to revert if needed.

ashley-support: Marking this as resolved with customer for now. I'll update ticket with bypass header and ETA for full fix (spec + timeline).

priya-sre: Closing notes: root cause = sync recursive JSON validation during tool routing causing serialization/queueing. Mitigation = bypass header + worker autoscale. Long-term = async validation, schema cache, compiled fast-path.

ashley-support: Thanks everyone. If anything pops up ping #incidents.
